items.title: Headlines for November 10, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## GOP Rep. Thomas Massie Introduces Articles of Impeachment Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 10, 2026 Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday for “high crimes and misdemeanors.” The eight impeachment articles accuse Hegseth of violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran even after both chambers of Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop. He’s also accused of illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” in attacks on boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, abducting Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. Congressmember Massie outlined the charges during a speech from the House floor. > Rep. Thomas Massie: “Wherefore, Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law, Peter Brian Hegseth thus warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States.” It’s expected the House will vote on Hegseth’s impeachment on Wednesday. Only a few Republican defectors would be needed for a simple majority, setting up a Senate trial on whether to remove Hegseth. On Monday, President Trump said he would stand by Hegseth if he’s impeached. ## Pentagon Retreats from Second U.K. Base Due to Alleged Threat from Iran Nov 10, 2026 The Wall Street Journal reports the Pentagon has evacuated aircraft from a second base in the United Kingdom due to another alleged threat from Iran. U.S. refueling tankers were reportedly moved from a base in Mildenhall on Monday. Last month, the Pentagon pulled B-1 bombers out of another British base. Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says two more ships, including a supertanker, are on fire near the Strait of Hormuz after using what Iranian officials have called an “unauthorized route.” Iran has claimed 11 strikes on ships over a 10-day span. The continued attacks on shipping came as Iran’s Foreign Ministry said it could reopen the strait within 48 hours if the U.S. agrees to Tehran’s list of demands. > Esmail Baghaei: “If the U.S. meets the demands put forward by Iran, the situation in the region could see a positive shift in as little as two days, and security in the Strait of Hormuz could also be restored.” On Monday, President Trump spoke with Qatar’s prime minister, who’s acted as a mediator in efforts to end the war. After the talks, Trump claimed there was “positive momentum” in negotiations for a deal with Iran. > President Donald Trump: “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes. Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.” Since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, Trump has claimed more than 40 times that the war was close to an end, that a deal was near, or that the war was already over. ## Trump Raises New Election Conspiracy Theory After Democrats Sweep Midterms Nov 10, 2026 Democrats are continuing to build on their historic wins in last week’s midterm elections as votes continue to be counted. In Mississippi, Scott Colom’s lead over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith has topped 2,500 votes, with just two batches of ballots left to be counted before a Friday deadline to certify the results. In Colorado, Republican Congressmember Lauren Boebert is trailing in her bid to hold on to her seat. On Monday, CNN projected Boebert will lose the race to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired U.S. Navy admiral who served on the National Security Council under President Joe Biden. On Monday, President Trump reversed his previous comment that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterm elections. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, “Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???” ... ## Senate Advances Bill to Speed Construction of Fossil Fuel Projects and Data Centers In more news from Capitol Hill, the Senate voted 73 to 25 Monday to take up a sweeping permitting reform bill. It was advanced by nearly every Republican and 22 Democrats. Environmental groups have called the legislation an “aggressive attack on federal environmental protections in order to facilitate rapid, unregulated development of fracked gas power plants, dirty fossil fuel pipelines, and expensive hyperscale data centers.” Meanwhile, Indigenous leaders, including New Mexico Governor-elect Deb Haaland, argue the bill would undermine tribal sovereignty.

items.title: Early Edition: November 10, 2026
items.excerpt: IRAN WAR President Trump yesterday reiterated that a renewed military campaign against Iran is “quite unlikely,” and “doesn’t seem to be necessary.” Trump’s comments were made on social media and at an impromptu press conference, and he added that “we want a long-term solution.” Trump told Reuters that Qatar and Saudi Arabia were eager for a peaceful solution to the Iran conflict but that the United States was ready to resume military strikes if necessary. Barak Ravid reports for Axios; Steve Holland reports for Reuters. Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani on social media yesterday described his talks with Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance about Iran as “positive.” The prime minister said he was “grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region.” France’s foreign minister today said the Qatari prime minister will make an unscheduled stop at the G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, France. Tara Suter reports for The Hill; John Irish reports for Reuters. IRAN WAR – OTHER DEVELOPMENTS France yesterday accused Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of being behind last month’s temperature-raising hack of French supermarket fridges and freezers. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression,” and added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless, while France today summoned Iran’s ambassador. Ella Kipling and Joe Tidy report for BBC News; John Irish reports for Reuters. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand at the G7 meeting today said Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities for their contribution to Iran’s nuclear activities and ballistic missile program. Anand said the measures were intended to restrict Iran’s access to funding and sensitive technology linked to its nuclear and missile programs. Rishabh Jaiswal reports for Reuters. The United States yesterday evacuated U.S. aircraft from the U.K. Royal Air Force base in Mildenhall in the wake of a threat from Iran, sources told the Wall Street Journal. The sources said the precise nature of the threat to RAF Mildenhall remains under discussion among U.S. officials. Shelby Holliday and Alexander Ward report. RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR Russian and Ukrainian officials today met in Abu Dhabi for their first U.S.-brokered talks since Feb. 2026. U.S. Special Envoy Jared Kushner told delegates that recent contacts with both sides had “really identified, narrowed the gaps,” and that Trump was committed to achieving peace. Roula Rouhana reports for Reuters. The White House is “cautiously optimistic” about the peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi this week, U.S. officials told Axios. A U.S. official said the “relations we have built with [Russian President Vladimir] Putin will be instrumental in these negotiations,” while another U.S. official said U.S. Special Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may travel to Ukraine and Russia to speak directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Putin. Barak Ravid reports. Russia believes the main thrust of U.S.-brokered peace talks on Ukraine should be seeking agreement on the main elements of a post-war security framework for Europe, a source in the Russian delegation told Reuters. The source said the Ukrainian settlement “is just one aspect of this wide-ranging discussion and is subordinate to the main objective – the creation of a comprehensive and indivisible security architecture for the entire continent.”

items.title: Fed officials open door to a half-point hike after inflation beats expectations By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King’s Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed’s inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller’s comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025. By mid-morning, market pricing reflected about a 15% chance of a half-point rate hike before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. Over the course of the day, traders also piled into bets the Fed would keep to its usual quarter-point rate hikes but deliver three of them by mid-2027, rather than two as seen before the data.

items.title: Fed’s Bowman says ’still work to do’ on inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 10 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Vice Chair of Supervision Michelle Bowman on Tuesday added her voice to the chorus of colleagues pointing to inflation as their biggest priority, though she stopped short of calling for interest-rate hikes and said she expects price pressures to abate next year as the effect of recent shocks wears off. "Today, I am seeing signs that inflation pressures are persisting, while labor market conditions appear to be firming," Bowman said in remarks prepared for delivery to the Council on Foreign Relations in Washington, DC. "This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2%." The core personal consumption expenditures price index likely rose 3.3% in October, she said, driven by higher energy prices and AI-related demand. But lack of progress on inflation, she added, has not been driven by the labor market, which has improved but is not overheated. As pressures from the AI buildout and the Middle East conflict "wane or unwind and with no inflationary pressures emerging in the labor market, my forecast is for core PCE inflation to move closer to 2% next year," she said. She cautioned that falling stock prices, rising bond yields and a stronger dollar have tightened financial conditions, creating possible risks to the economy, which has strengthened this year. "The benefit of additional policy tightening has to be carefully weighed against its costs for interest-rate-sensitive sectors," Bowman said. "Time will help us learn more about the durability of momentum in AI-related demand and the evolution of geopolitical risks, both of which could be critical in the months ahead for setting our policy stance."

items.title: Trump backs Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Republicans select new congressional leaders: Morning Rundown

Trump said at an impromptu news conference yesterday that the FBI is now investigating Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the managing director of Singaporean tech company Megaspeed. The pair are not related. U.S. intelligence agencies now believe she is a Chinese spy. Trump said he called Huang “to see if he’s feeling all right,” and Huang told him “he had absolutely no idea that person was a spy.” Trump added, “I really believe him.” Meanwhile, a person familiar with the matter said the Justice Department told the Commerce Department to pause its investigation into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s AI chips into China.

items.title: Entertainment News (11/10/26)
items.excerpt: ## We Are Imaginary releases music video FILIPINO indie-rock band We Are Imaginary has dropped the official music video for “Are We There Yet?,” the latest single from their 2026 self-titled album. Directed by Jam Lasin of Cream Flower, the music video captures the band in their jamming element, stitching together performances, candid moments, and visual references that pay tribute to their 18-year career as an underground force in the Filipino independent music scene. The music video also traces the highs and lows of band life. The track, which retains the post-punk guitar sensibilities of its original demo, is available on all streaming platforms. ## 2 Valid IDs hits P100-million box office milestone POWERED by word of mouth and a growing audience campaign, the small independent film 2 Valid IDs starring Marietta Subong (a.k.a. Pokwang) and directed by Ma-an L. Asuncion-Dagñalan, has crossed the P100-million mark at the Philippine box office. It has become one of the highest-grossing films in Cinemalaya history. Now on its fourth week in cinemas, the film generated interest online for its relatable storyline. Written by Abet Pagdadaganan Raz, 2 Valid IDs follows Sylvia, a poor provincial farmer trying to secure financial assistance for her hospitalized husband, made difficult due to frustrating bureaucratic processes that require two valid government-issued IDs. At Cinemalaya 2026, it won three awards: Best Actress for Ms. Subong, the Special Jury Award, and the Audience Choice Award. ## The Lord of the Rings concert coming in 2027 FILM Concerts Philippines has revealed that they will be presenting The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert on March 4, 5, and 6, 2027, at The Theatre at Solaire, Parañaque City. As Peter Jackson’s acclaimed film plays on the big screen, Howard Shore’s Academy Award-winning score will be performed live by the 247-member ensemble of the Filharmonika Orchestra, the Philippine Madrigal Singers’ adult and boys’ choirs, and soloist Malena Rampi, under the baton of conductor Reuben Blundell. This will mark the largest ensemble Film Concerts Philippines has assembled to date. Since the film’s premiere in 2008, The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert has been performed by leading orchestras worldwide. Exclusive pre-sale access for Film Concerts Philippines community members is ongoing until Nov. 11, with public ticket sales beginning Nov. 20. ## Zoë Kravitz, John C. Reilly star in How to Rob a Bank THE upcoming film How to Rob a Bank kicks off with a gang of masked livestreaming bank robbers turning the FBI on its head. In the middle of the investigation is special agent John West, played by John C. Reilly, who forms an unlikely partnership with a software engineer on house arrest, played by Zoë Kravitz. Their combined skills are needed to take the viral criminals down. How to Rob A Bank also stars Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Christian Slater, and Pete Davidson. The film arrives in Philippine cinemas on Nov. 11. ## LEYO releases new EP FILIPINO singer-songwriter LEYO has reimagined the Filipino harana (serenade) with modern sensibilities in Akda sa Pag-alala, a six-track EP released under Sony Music Entertainment. Blending classic OPM, acoustic pop, and R&B, it is a personal collection shaped by affection, longing, vulnerability, and self-discovery. It balances guitar riffs and bass lines with jazzy, bossa nova-lite inflections, borrowing from a range of influences like The Beatles, Stevie Wonder, the APO Hiking Society, and the Manila Sound. The EP’s producers include 2026 Awit Awards winner Brian Lotho, Rain Santana, and LEYO himself. Akda sa Pag-alala is out now on all digital music platforms worldwide. ## George Michael concert film coming in Nov. GEORGE MICHAEL Entertainment, in partnership with Mercury Studios, has announced the start of the worldwide theatrical release of a brand-new, never-before-seen film titled George Michael: The Faith Tour, with screenings beginning on Nov. 11. Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into an era-defining artist. Directed by Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once-lost film has been restored and remastered, transforming archival footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film into a cinematic experience. ... ## Dune, Dune: Part Two return for a limited time TO RELIVE the journey before experiencing the third and final installment of the film series this December, Dune and Dune: Part Two will be back in cinemas and IMAX for one week starting Nov. 11. The screenings will include an exclusive sneak peek of Dune: Part Three, the conclusion to Denis Villeneuve’s Dune trilogy.

items.excerpt: To begin with, Ramayana created history and recorded its highest single day collection on its first Monday post release ... ## Bomb Threat To Madhya Pradesh High Court Mentions Diljit Dosanjh's Indore Concert The Madhya Pradesh High Court's Gwalior bench received an email threatening to blow up its premises, which also referred to singer Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert in Indore on November 15, police said. Security at the court has been strengthened, while police teams are investigating the origin of the email and attempting to identify the sender. This comes after three schools and the Indore Mayor's office reportedly received similar threats linked to the concert. Amid the developments, Dosanjh said on Tuesday that the event would go ahead as scheduled. (PTI) ... ## Kunal Kapoor Says Ramayana's Success Could Encourage Filmmakers To Take Bigger Risks Actor Kunal Kapoor, who plays Lord Indra in Ramayana: Part One, believes the film's success could encourage filmmakers to take greater creative and financial risks in Indian cinema. In an interview with PTI, Kapoor said it was important for the ambitious project to recover its investment and perform well at the box office, as it could give others the confidence to pursue larger projects. He also expressed interest in seeing Lord Indra get a standalone film, saying the character has the potential to build its own universe. ... ## Padma Shri Sitar Maestro Pandit Manilal Nag Dies At 87 In Kolkata Renowned sitar maestro and Padma Shri awardee Pandit Manilal Nag, a celebrated exponent of the Bishnupur gharana, died at a private hospital in Kolkata on Monday night. He was 87 and had been suffering from age-related ailments. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari condoled his demise, describing it as the end of an era in Indian classical music. Nag received the Padma Shri in 2020 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2001 for his contribution to music. (PTI)
